subtopics.title: What a Control Account Is and Why We Need One

questions.question: What is the relationship between the Debtors Control account and the Debtors Ledger?
options: The control account shows detail; the Debtors Ledger shows totals
The control account shows totals; the Debtors Ledger shows each debtor's detail
They record different transactions entirely
The Debtors Ledger replaces the control account at year end

questions.question: Why does the Debtors Control account normally have a debit balance?
options: Because debtors are an asset — money owed to the business
Because debtors are a liability — money the business owes
Because expenses are recorded there
Because the bank column is always positive

questions.question: At month end, the Debtors Control balance must agree with:
options: The total of the Cash Receipts Journal
The balance of the Bank account
The total of the list of individual debtors' balances
The Creditors Control balance

subtopics.title: Posting the Debit Side — When Debtors Owe Us More

questions.question: The Debtors Journal total of R48 200 is posted to the Debtors Control account as:
options: A credit, because sales are income
A debit, because credit sales make debtors owe the business more
Forty separate debit entries, one per invoice
A debit to the Bank account

questions.question: Why are individual invoices never posted to the Debtors Control account?
options: Invoices are not valid source documents
The control account only receives journal totals; detail goes to the personal accounts
Invoices are posted to the Creditors Ledger instead
Individual invoices are only posted at year end

questions.question: The account opened with a balance b/d of R15 400 on the debit side. What does this figure represent?
options: Cash received from debtors in May
The amount debtors still owed the business at the end of the previous month
The June credit sales total
The amount the business owes its creditors

subtopics.title: Posting the Credit Side — When Debtors Owe Us Less

questions.question: Which set of items is posted to the CREDIT side of the Debtors Control account?
options: Credit sales, opening balance, bad debts
Receipts from debtors, debtors allowances, bad debts written off
Credit sales and receipts from debtors
Only the closing balance

questions.question: Using the lesson's figures — debit side R15 400 + R48 200, credit side R31 500 + R2 300 + R900 — what is the closing balance of the Debtors Control account?
When the R900 bad debt is written off, the contra account for the credit to Debtors Control is:
options: Bank, because the money was received
Sales, because the sale is cancelled
Bad Debts, an expense absorbed by the business
Capital, because the owner pays for it

questions.question: Goods returned by a debtor (recorded in the Debtors Allowances Journal) are credited to Debtors Control because:
options: The return cancels part of the original credit sale, so the debtor owes less
Returns increase what the debtor owes
Returns are treated as cash received
The goods become a donation

subtopics.title: The Agreement Check and the Creditors Mirror Image

questions.question: The control balance is R28 900 but the debtors list totals R29 800. What does this tell the bookkeeper?
options: The business made a loss of R900
An error exists somewhere between the detail and the summary records
The difference must be written off as a bad debt
Nothing — small differences are acceptable

questions.question: In the Creditors Control account, a payment made to a supplier is posted as:
options: A credit, because payments increase the liability
A debit, because paying a creditor reduces what the business owes
A debit to the Debtors Control account
No entry — payments to creditors bypass the control account

questions.question: Why does the Creditors Control account normally carry a credit balance?
options: Because creditors are an asset of the business
Because purchases are always paid in cash
Because creditors are a liability — amounts the business owes
Because the account records income
